All right. So, in terms of the Privacy Act, it came into effect on
1 December 2020. Its purpose is to protect and promote
people's right to privacy over their personal information.
It applies to individuals and agencies.
And when we say agencies, we mean
agencies that decide to collect personal information for a particular
purpose. And the Privacy Commissioner is an independent Crown
entity, and he has a range of powers under the act,
including resolving complaints and enforcing compliance.
The act is principles based rather than rules based.
And the principles are intended to be flexible and proportionate,
both to the range of agencies or organizations the act applies to,
and based on the nature of the information they hold.
So the act is quite context specific.
In terms of the commissioner's role,
the commissioner has a role in terms of resolving individual complaints.
So any person can make a complaint alleging that
an action of an agency is an interference with their privacy,
and then the commissioner will decide whether or not to investigate that
complaint. And the complaint may lead to a settlement
between the complainant and the agency, an assurance
from the agency that the action will not be repeated.
The commissioner could investigate the complaint.
The commissioner can make a referral to the Director of Human Rights,
Review Tribunal proceedings.
And the tribunal, the Human Rights Review Tribunal, may award
remedies to an individual if satisfied that there has been a
privacy interference,
including damages up to a maximum of $350,000.
Then there are
enforcement powers available to the commissioner.
So I've just talked about the individual complaints that they
deal with. But in terms of the enforcement powers of the commissioner, they can
inquire into any matter that appears to be an infringement with the privacy
of individuals,
can investigate a complaint or a matter about which a complaint may be made
under the act. They can issue compliance notices to agencies if they
consider the agency has breached the act, a privacy
principle, or a relevant code of practice.
And the compliance notice
can sets out the nature of the breach, and then it can direct agencies
to take specific steps to remedy the breach.
And compliance notices are enforceable through the Human Rights Review Tribunal.
And failure to comply with the tribunal is an
offense. It's a criminal offense punishable by a fine of up to

We've just conducted our 2026

privacy in general are deepening and diversifying.

seen over recent years.

need for greater enforcement powers under the Act, with support
from over 70% of the respondents.
